title: Immutable evidence sideband PRD - proposal
content:
Status: DRAFT - exploratory PRD / technical proposal for a lightweight immutable evidence sideband to support customer-managed networking and approval flows.

Summary:
This document proposes a minimal, append-only "sideband" evidence channel that runs alongside normal VPC/on-prem change workflows to provide a tamper-evident, compact forensic artifact for approval gates, sampling, and post-incident reconstruction. The goal is to give customers and Redwood operations a small, cryptographically-signed snapshot of: (a) what change was requested, (b) who authorized it, (c) the pre/post observable fingerprint, and (d) a short retention-safe index that allows efficient query without retaining full telemetry.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Private deployments require robust evidence for audits and incident response, but full telemetry retention is cost-prohibitive for many customers.
- Current approval flows are asynchronous and can be opaque: ticket links + screenshots are fragile.
- Operators need a way to validate that an approved change actually matches what was applied, without storing large packet captures or full configuration dumps.

Principles and constraints:
- Minimal data: keep sideband payloads compact (<= 4KB per event by default).
- Append-only and signed: each event must be cryptographically verifiable (client signs, Redwood signs where applicable).
- Customer sovereignty: sideband must be transportable to customer-managed storage (S3/GCS) or Redwood escrow depending on contract.
- Configurable sampling: default 100% for critical changes, sampling for routine changes to limit cost.
- Privacy-aware: avoid including raw credentials, PII, or large configs in payload; include hashes instead.
- Offline-friendly: support customers with limited egress by batching and offline handoff.

User personas / user stories:
- Platform engineer (customer): "I need a compact certificate that shows my network admin approved this VPC route change and the exact commit hash / manifest applied, so I can present it to my compliance team."
- SRE/Oncall (Redwood): "When a private deploy customer reports degradation after a rollout, I want a searchable, signed evidence item to validate approval and timeline before escalating."
- Auditor: "I want to sample a set of approval events and match them against changelogs; each evidence item must prove integrity and origin."

Scope (what this PRD covers):
- Sideband event schema proposal, signing model, transport options, and retention presets.
- Integration points with approval gates and onboarding flows (self-service and Concierge).
- UI/Console surface for searching evidence items and downloading proof bundles.
- Lightweight query API to surface evidence items to customer and Redwood support.

Non-goals:
- Full packet or full-configuration backups.
- Replacing SIEM or heavyweight forensic tooling.
- Advanced legal custody solutions (we will provide basic escrow but full legal escrow flows are out of scope for v1).

Requirements (functional):
1) Event schema: each sideband event must include:
   - event_id (UUID v4)
   - timestamp (ISO-8601)
   - change_type (route_update, firewall_rule, software_rollout, operator-override)
   - change_reference (ticket id, git commit, operator session id) or hash of manifest
   - requester (principal id) and approver(s) (list of principal ids)
   - approval_policy_id (if gating policy recorded)
   - pre_state_hash and post_state_hash (SHA-256 of normalized baseline snapshot)
   - short human summary (<= 280 chars)
   - signatures: requester_signature, approver_signatures (base64), redwood_ingest_signature (optional)
   - retention_ttl_label (ephemeral|short|standard|long)
2) Signing model: support multiple signing roots — customer KMS (recommended) and Redwood-signed fallback. Signatures must cover canonicalized payload. Provide verification helpers in SDKs.
3) Transport: 3 delivery modes — direct push to customer-managed bucket (preferred), push to Redwood escrow with encrypted-at-rest storage, or hybrid (push to Redwood but mirror to customer on request).
4) Sampling and policy: default policy per customer with override rules: critical changes always 100%, routine optionally sampled at 1-10% depending on contract tier. Sampling decisions must be recorded as a sideband meta-event.
5) Query API: read-only endpoints to list, filter by time/change_type/principal/ticket, and to fetch signed bundle (payload + signatures + verification metadata). API must support audit exports (zip of multiple items).
6) Console: evidence search, download bundle, and evidence timeline pinned to route/tenant pages.
7) Forensics quick-check: a built-in verification flow that compares evidence item pre/post hashes against live ephemeral snapshots (if customer permits remote probe) to assert equivalence.

Non-functional requirements:
- Per-event budget: default size target <= 4KB; allow larger events for exceptional cases but mark as 'bulk'.
- Ingest latency: sideband event must be persisted and acknowledged within 10s of change completion for hosted transport; longer acceptable for offline/batched modes ( <= 5m ).
- Verification speed: verification helper should verify a bundle in < 200ms for typical event sizes.
- Retention controls: support retention presets and legal-hold tagging that overrides TTL.

Privacy and data minimization:
- Do not include raw IP addresses where possible; use network-normalized labels + fingerprints.
- Credentials/keys must be replaced with hashes.
- Allow opt-in for including small diffs or full manifests; default to hashes only.

Approval gate integration (high level flow):
- Pre-change: admin opens change ticket -> change manifest generated -> sideband pre-event created and signed by requester (optionally by local operator agent).
- Approval: approvers sign the sideband via the console or an approval API; approval signature appended.
- Apply: after approval, change is applied; post_state snapshot computed by a lightweight comparator agent and appended to event (post_state_hash).
- Persist: event sent to chosen transport; ingest returns final_ack.
- Post-change: evidence item is discoverable via API/Console. If sampling was applied, metadata records sampling_decision and sampling_seed.

Agent/edge component responsibilities:
- A small sideband agent runs in customer environment (or as part of sidecar) and: collects normalized pre/post snapshots, canonicalizes payload, asks local KMS to sign, and pushes to transport.
- Fallback mode: if local signing not available, agent requests temporary signing token from Redwood with short TTL; agent signs locally and pushes.

API contract (sketch):
- POST /evidence/v1/events  -> submit event (signed payload).
- GET /evidence/v1/events?tenant=...&from=...&type=... -> list events.
- GET /evidence/v1/events/{id}/bundle -> download signed bundle (payload + signatures + verification instructions).
- GET /evidence/v1/verify/{id}?probe=true -> run verification check (subject to permissions).

Monitoring and alerts:
- Ingest error rate > 0.1% -> alert ops.
- Missing post_state_hash for critical changes -> alert security-owner.
- Sampling drift (actual vs configured) > 5% -> alert product.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiment): internal-only pilot with three friendly-customer participants. Manual SDK usage, Redwood escrow only.
- Phase 1 (beta): customer-managed bucket transport, sidecar agent v0.1, console search read-only.
- Phase 2 (general availability): retention presets, legal-hold, verification UI, sampling policies, open SDKs.

Acceptance criteria (v1):
- Event schema stable and documented.
- Sidecar agent can produce a signed event and successfully push to S3 and receive ack.
- Console can search and download bundles for pilot tenants.
- Verification helper validates signatures and hashes for at least 95% of pilot events.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: customers treat sideband as substitute for full logging and lose critical telemetry. Mitigation: explicit docs and onboard messaging that sideband is complementary, not a replacement.
- Risk: key management complexity across customer KMS implementations. Mitigation: provide standard adapters (AWS/GCP/Azure) and fallback short-lived tokens.
- Risk: regulatory/legal requirements for custody. Mitigation: provide escrow option and contract language for higher tiers.

Open questions (design decisions to make):
- Should sideband events include an optional encrypted payload field for redwood-escrow-only customers who want a full manifest? (tradeoff: size vs. usefulness)
- What is the default sampling rate per tier? Suggested: free tier 1%, standard 5%, enterprise 20% with overrides.
- Do we allow chaining events (for multi-step changes) or force a single canonical event per change?

Next steps / owners:
- Product: scope & finalize schema (owner: Maya Chen) - 2 sprints.
- Infra: prototype push-to-bucket and short-lived token flow (owner: Arjun Patel) - 3 weeks.
- Applied ML / Forensics: build verification helper and canonicalization heuristics (owner: Lina Gomez) - 3 sprints.
- Security: threat model and KMS adapter review (owner: Samir Bhatt) - 2 weeks.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally conservative: small payloads, signatures, and transport options. Focus is on auditability and cost practicality for customers who run private or on-prem deployments.
- We're trying to avoid a heavy-handed SIEM-like solution while still enabling meaningful audits and fast triage.

Appendix (examples):
- Example event (pseudo-canonical):
  { event_id: "uuid-1234", timestamp: "2024-10-03T14:22:11Z", change_type: "firewall_rule", change_reference: "ticket-PD-1084", requester: "user:m.chen@redwood.com", approvers: ["user:a.patel@cust.com"], pre_state_hash: "sha256:abcd...", post_state_hash: "sha256:ef01...", summary: "open port 22 for bastion for migration window", signatures: { requester: "base64sig...", approver: "base64sig..." }, retention_ttl_label: "standard" }

Please review schema fields and signing model; looking for feedback on retention presets and sampling defaults.
